mainTopic: Why רבי שמעון rules differently in the two cases of the misunderstood נזירות; and whether a friend's 'וַאֲנִי' takes on all or part of another's vow
overview: The amud begins by explaining why רבי שמעון seems lenient in one case of the משנה and strict in the other. The first answer is that רבי שמעון holds you are a נזיר only if you accept every prohibition. In the רישא the man accepted only part of נזירות, so he is not a נזיר. In the סיפא he accepted all of it and asked to be released from one part, so he stays a נזיר. A second answer says the argument is about נדרי אונסין. רבנן follow שמואל, who holds that such vows fall away by themselves. רבי שמעון follows רב אסי, who holds that they need a חכם. Then a new משנה teaches about two friends who each vow to be a נזיר and to pay for another נזיר's shaving. The גמרא asks whether a bare 'וַאֲנִי' takes on the whole statement or only part of it. רבא proves from the משנה's wording that it covers only becoming a נזיר. He defends this against רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's challenge from the half-נזיר case. Finally, a new teaching of רבי יוחנן about a man and his messenger begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The first case: he accepted only part of נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The רישא is a man who vowed נזירות from only one item. רבנן say that still makes him a full נזיר, so he is forbidden. רבי שמעון says you are only a נזיר if you accept all the prohibitions, so he is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first case is where he vowed נזירות about just one thing. According to רבנן, who say that even if he vowed about only one of them he is a נזיר, he is forbidden. According to רבי שמעון, who says he is not a נזיר until he vows about all of them, he is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining the first case of the משנה. It applies each side's rule about how much of נזירות a person must accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who thought a נזיר may drink wine never really accepted the wine prohibition, so he vowed about only part of נזירות. For רבנן, accepting even one part makes him a full נזיר, so wine is forbidden too. For רבי שמעון, partial acceptance creates no נזירות at all, so he is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
He vowed נזירות about only one item
Not until he vows about all of them (רבי שמעון's rule)

phrases.english: The first clause is a case where he vowed נזירות from one thing,
phrases.notes: This is the man who thought a נזיר may drink wine, so he only took on part of נזירות.

phrases.english: according to the Rabbis, who say

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲפִילּוּ לֹא נָזַר אֶלָּא מֵאַחַת מֵהֶן —
phrases.english: that even if he vowed נזירות from only one of them,
he is a נזיר, and he is forbidden.
According to רבי שמעון, who says
he is not a נזיר until he vows from all of them, he is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer to the contradiction in רבי שמעון's rulings, which the גמרא raised just before this point
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two clauses into different case setups
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון seems to permit in one case and forbid in a nearly identical case
steps.terutzMaskana: In the רישא he accepted only part of נזירות, so by רבי שמעון's rule he is not a נזיר at all

steps.title: The second case: he accepted everything, then asked release from one
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא is a man who vowed נזירות from all the items, then asked a חכם to release him from one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last clause is where he vowed about all of them, and asked to be released from one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the second case of the משנה differently from the first. This sets up how each side will rule on it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the man knew wine was forbidden, so he fully accepted all of נזירות. His mistake was thinking a חכם would release him from wine alone. So this case is about releasing one part of a complete vow, not about a partial vow.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
He asked a חכם to release his vow

phrases.english: The last clause is where he vowed from all of them,
and asked to be released from one.
phrases.notes: This is the man who thought the חכמים would let him have wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching case setup for the second clause
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is a full vow followed by a request to release one part

steps.title: How each side rules on releasing one part
steps.stepSummary: For רבנן, releasing one part frees him from the whole נזירות. For רבי שמעון, releasing one part does nothing until he is released from all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבנן, who say that even one item makes him a נזיר, when he is released from one of them he becomes fully permitted. According to רבי שמעון, who says he must vow about all of them, even when he is released from that one he stays forbidden until he is released from all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies each side's rule to the second case and shows that it reverses the outcome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, any one part is enough to hold the whole נזירות, so removing one part removes all of it. For רבי שמעון, the vow is built from all the parts together, so taking away one part does not undo it. That is why רבי שמעון is strict here even though he was lenient in the first case.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, who say

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לֹא נָזַר אֶלָּא מֵאַחַת מֵהֶן הָוֵי נָזִיר,
phrases.english: that even if he vowed from only one of them he is a נזיר,
when he is released from one of them, he is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר עַד שֶׁיַּזִּיר מִכּוּלָּם,
phrases.english: According to רבי שמעון, who says not until he vows from all of them,
even when he is released from that one,
he is not permitted until he is released from all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי אֲפִילּוּ לֹא נָזַר אֶלָּא מֵאַחַת מֵהֶן הָוֵי נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies both opinions to the case defined in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: The same rule produces opposite results in different cases
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון is consistent: a vow made from all the parts needs release from all the parts

steps.title: That is why רבי שמעון forbids in the second case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up: this is why the משנה says רבי שמעון forbids in the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of this, the משנה teaches: and רבי שמעון forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the first answer by tying it back to the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The apparent contradiction is gone. רבי שמעון has one rule, that נזירות needs all the parts. It makes him lenient when the man accepted only some, and strict when the man accepted all and was released from only one.
steps.whatToRemember: First answer: רבי שמעון holds you are a נזיר only if you accept all the prohibitions. So a partial vow means no נזירות (lenient), and a full vow stays until every part is released (strict). רבנן hold the opposite on both counts.

phrases.english: Because of this it teaches:
and רבי שמעון forbids.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון's two rulings come from one consistent rule

steps.title: Second answer: the dispute is about vows broken by forces beyond his control
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another explanation: רבנן and רבי שמעון argue about נדרי אונסין, and their argument matches the dispute of שמואל and רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: they disagree about vows forced by circumstances beyond one's control, and it is the same as the argument between שמואל and רב אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a completely new way to explain the משנה. This step only names the topic; the details come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the 'all of them' rule, this answer places the argument in the area of נדרי אונסין. It links the disagreement to an existing dispute between שמואל and רב אסי, which the גמרא has not explained yet. The next step brings the source text for this topic.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Vows broken by circumstances beyond one's control

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
they disagree about vows of circumstances beyond one's control,
and it is in the dispute of שמואל and רב אסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּנִדְרֵי אוֹנָסִין קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent explanation of the same משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the משנה's dispute to an already known dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument in the משנה is really about נדרי אונסין

steps.title: The משנה of the four vows the Sages permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: the חכמים permitted four kinds of vows: vows of urging, vows of exaggeration, mistaken vows, and vows broken by forces beyond one's control.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: The Sages permitted four kinds of vows: vows of urging, vows of exaggeration, mistaken vows, and vows of circumstances beyond one's control.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source text where נדרי אונסין appear. This sets up the dispute between שמואל and רב אסי that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה lists four kinds of vows that the חכמים permitted. The last one, נדרי אונסין, is the category the second answer depends on. Whether these vows still need a חכם to release them is exactly what שמואל and רב אסי argue about in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
The Sages permitted four kinds of vows:
Vows of urging. Vows of exaggeration.
Mistaken vows. Vows of circumstances beyond one's control.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source text for the נדרי אונסין topic named in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים permitted four kinds of vows: urging, exaggeration, mistaken, and those broken by forces beyond one's control

steps.title: רב אסי: the four vows still need a חכם
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that the four vows the חכמים permitted still need a request to a חכם before they are released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: these four vows need a request to the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first side of the argument promised in step 5. רב אסי says the four permitted vows are not released by themselves. A person must go to a חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the משנה listed four vows that the חכמים "permitted." רב אסי reads this as permission for a חכם to release them, not as automatic release. Until someone asks a חכם, the vow still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A request to a חכם to release a vow
The אמורא who holds these vows need a חכם
The אמורא who reports רב אסי's ruling

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said:
These four vows
phrases.notes: These are the four vows from the משנה quoted in step 6: urging, exaggeration, mistakes, and forces beyond one's control.

phrases.english: require a request to the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב אסי's ruling on the four vows quoted in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four permitted vows are not released until a person asks a חכם.

steps.title: שמואל objects: the משנה says the חכמים already permitted them
steps.stepSummary: שמואל challenges רב אסי. The משנה's words "הִתִּירוּ חֲכָמִים" mean the vows are already released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: when I told this to שמואל, he answered me: the תנא teaches "the חכמים permitted," and you say they need a request to the חכמים?!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes back against רב אסי's ruling. He points to the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The חכמים permitted" sounds like the release has already happened. שמואל holds that no visit to a חכם is needed, so these vows are void by themselves. This is the second side of the argument mentioned in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא teaches, pointing to the wording of the משנה
The אמורא who holds these vows are released automatically

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The "I" here is רב יהודה, telling over what happened.

phrases.english: he said to me:
The tanna teaches "the Sages permitted,"
and you say
they require a request to the Sages?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל argues against רב אסי's ruling from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that the four vows need a request to a חכם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the חכמים already "permitted" these vows. That suggests they are released automatically, with no request needed.

steps.title: רבנן follow שמואל, רבי שמעון follows רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: The argument between רבנן and רבי שמעון in the earlier משנה is the same as the argument between שמואל and רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן hold like שמואל, and רבי שמעון holds like רב אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second explanation it started in step 5. It matches each side of the earlier משנה to one of these אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא of the earlier משנה, the man's נזירות is treated as a kind of נדרי אונסין. רבנן say it falls away by itself, like שמואל. רבי שמעון says he stays a נזיר until a חכם releases him, like רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows broken by forces beyond one's control

steps.whatToRemember: Second explanation of the earlier argument: רבנן say a vow broken by force is void by itself (like שמואל). רבי שמעון says it still needs a חכם (like רב אסי).

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold like Shmuel.
And Rabbi Shimon holds like Rav Asi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the שמואל and רב אסי argument from steps 7 and 8 to explain the argument of רבנן and רבי שמעון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument of רבנן and רבי שמעון is about whether a vow broken by force needs a חכם. רבנן follow שמואל (no), and רבי שמעון follows רב אסי (yes).

steps.title: New משנה: vowing to be a נזיר and to pay for another נזיר's shaving
steps.stepSummary: A man vows to be a נזיר and to pay for another נזיר's shaving, and his friend says the same. If they are smart, each pays for the other's shaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says "I am a נזיר and I take on myself to shave a נזיר," and his friend hears and says "And I, and I take on myself to shave a נזיר": if they are clever, they shave each other. If not, they shave other נזירים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Two people each vow to be a נזיר and also to pay for some other נזיר's shaving קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "To shave a נזיר" means paying for the קרבנות a נזיר brings when his נזירות ends. Smart friends cover each other's shaving, so the extra promise costs nothing more. Otherwise each must also pay for some other נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: To pay for a נזיר's shaving קרבנות

steps.confusionAlert: "Shaving a נזיר" here does not mean cutting his hair yourself. It means paying for the קרבנות he brings at his shaving.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
"I am hereby a nazir
and it is upon me to shave a nazir,"
and his friend heard and said
"And I, and it is upon me to shave a nazir."
If they were clever
they shave each other.
phrases.notes: Each one pays for the other's קרבנות, which takes care of both promises.

phrases.english: And if not,
they shave other nezirim.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר וְעָלַי לְגַלֵּחַ נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people who each vowed to be a נזיר and to pay for a נזיר's shaving can cover each other's shaving if they are smart. Otherwise each must pay for another נזיר's shaving.

steps.title: What if the friend only said "and me"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the friend's "וַאֲנִי" copies the whole statement or only half of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if his friend heard and only said "And I," what is the law? Does "And I" mean the whole statement, or maybe only half of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the משנה. In the משנה the friend repeated everything, but what if he only said "וַאֲנִי"?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first man said two things: "I am a נזיר" and "I will pay for a נזיר's shaving." Maybe a bare "וַאֲנִי" takes on both. Or maybe it only takes on one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: Gemara:
It was asked of them:
If his friend heard and said "And I," what is the law?
Does "And I" refer to the whole statement,
or perhaps it refers to half the statement?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שָׁמַע חֲבֵירוֹ וְאָמַר וַאֲנִי, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case the משנה in step 10 does not cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a bare "וַאֲנִי" takes on both parts of the first man's vow or only one part.

steps.title: If only half, which half?
steps.stepSummary: If "וַאֲנִי" only covers half, does it go on the first part (being a נזיר) or the last part (paying for a נזיר's shaving)?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it only means half the statement: is it the first part or the last part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a follow-up question. It is setting up the possibilities that the discussion will need to decide between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part is "I am a נזיר," and the last part is "I will pay for a נזיר's shaving." Maybe "וַאֲנִי" grabs the first idea. Or maybe it grabs the words said right before it, which is the last part.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say, if you decide

phrases.english: If you will say
it refers to half the statement:
the first part, or the last part?
phrases.notes: The first part is "I am a נזיר"; the last part is "I will pay for shaving a נזיר."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר אַפַּלְגֵיהּ דְּדִיבּוּרָא מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up that assumes the "half" answer from step 11 and asks which half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If "וַאֲנִי" covers only half, whether it covers becoming a נזיר or paying for a נזיר's shaving.

steps.title: The extra words in the משנה show that 'and I' covers only half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the friend's words in the משנה, 'וַאֲנִי וְעָלַי לְגַלֵּחַ נָזִיר'. Since he had to add 'וְעָלַי', it proves that 'וַאֲנִי' alone covers only half of the first statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the friend says 'And I, and it is on me to pay for a נזיר's shaving.' If they are smart, each pays for the other's shaving. Since he says 'And I, and on me,' we learn that 'and I' only takes on half of the statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11 by reading the exact words of the משנה closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'וַאֲנִי' already copied the whole statement, the friend would not need to add 'וְעָלַי'. The fact that the משנה has him add more words shows that 'וַאֲנִי' by itself only takes on half.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; it brings a source as a proof
To pay for the קרבנות a נזיר brings when he shaves at the end

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And I, and it is on me to shave a nazir,'
phrases.notes: This is the friend's answer in the משנה from step 10. 'To shave a nazir' means paying for his shaving קרבנות.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ פִּקְחִים מְגַלְּחִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: if they are smart, they pay for each other's shaving.
Since it says 'And I, and on me' —

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ וַאֲנִי אַפַּלְגֵיהּ דְּדִיבּוּרָא אָמְרִי.
phrases.english: learn from this that 'and I' is said about half of the statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof to answer the question from step 11
steps.raayaObject: That 'וַאֲנִי' covers only half of the statement
steps.raayaSupportSource: The friend's extra word 'וְעָלַי' in the משנה

steps.title: Agreed it is half, but which half?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof that 'וַאֲנִי' covers half. But the question from step 12 remains: the first half or the last half? The next step answers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it means half the statement. But is it the first part or the last part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proof and then brings back the question that is still open. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only showed that 'וַאֲנִי' is not the whole statement. It did not show which half it covers, so the second question from step 12 still needs an answer.

phrases.english: Yes, it means half of the statement;
however: on the first part, or on the last part?
phrases.notes: The first part is 'I am a נזיר.' The last part is 'I will pay for a נזיר's shaving.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 13 but shows that the question from step 12 is still open
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'וַאֲנִי' cover the first half or the last half of the statement?

steps.title: 'And I' goes on the first part: becoming a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה answers this too. The friend adds 'וְעָלַי לְגַלֵּחַ' (the paying part), so 'וַאֲנִי' must cover the first part, becoming a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from the משנה itself. Since he says 'and on me to shave,' we learn that 'and I' means the beginning of the statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers which half 'וַאֲנִי' covers, using the same words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words the friend adds are exactly the paying part, 'עָלַי לְגַלֵּחַ'. So the half he still had to add is the last part. That means 'וַאֲנִי' must have covered the first part, becoming a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: From it itself, meaning from this same משנה

steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading, 'וַאֲנִי' alone makes the friend a נזיר. Taking on the payment needs the extra words 'וְעָלַי לְגַלֵּחַ'.

phrases.english: From it itself: since it says 'and on me to shave,'
learn from this: 'and I' —
means the beginning of the statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וַאֲנִי' goes on the first part of the statement, becoming a נזיר

steps.title: רב הונא says 'and I' could cover everything
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks רבא how he knows this. Maybe 'וַאֲנִי' covers the whole statement, and 'וְעָלַי' only explains it: 'it is on me, this whole matter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רבא: How do you know this? I can tell you that 'and I' covers the whole statement. And the word 'and on me' just means 'this matter is on me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back on the proof. He offers another way to read the extra word 'וְעָלַי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on 'וְעָלַי' being a new, extra commitment. רב הונא says it may just be the friend spelling out what he already took on. If so, the extra words prove nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know it is so?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rava:
From where do you know it is so?
Really, I can tell you
that 'and I' goes on the whole statement,
and if you point to 'and on me,'
what is he saying? 'And it is on me, this matter.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 13 to 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that 'וַאֲנִי' covers only half
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'וְעָלַי' may only explain what he already took on, not add something new

steps.title: Proof from the half-נזיר case in the next משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא backs up his reading. In the next משנה, a man vows to pay for half a נזיר's shaving, and his friend says 'וַאֲנִי עָלַי לְגַלֵּחַ חֲצִי נָזִיר'. There is only one thing there to accept, so 'עָלַי' must just mean 'this matter'. The same is true here.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you don't say this, then look at the last case taught: 'It is on me to pay for shaving half a נזיר,' and his friend heard and said, 'And I, it is on me to pay for shaving half a נזיר.' Are there two things there? No. So what does 'on me' mean? 'This matter is on me.' Here too, when he says 'on me,' he means this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings a case where 'עָלַי' clearly cannot be adding a second part, to show it can just be explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the half-נזיר case the first man made only one commitment, so there is no 'other half' for 'עָלַי' to add. Still, the friend says 'עָלַי'. So 'עָלַי' can be plain explaining wording, and it proves nothing in our case either.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if you do not say so
Half a נזיר: paying for half of a נזיר's shaving קרבנות

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then what is taught in the later case,
'It is on me to shave half a nazir,'
and his friend heard and said,
'And I, it is on me to shave half a nazir,'
there, are there two things?
Rather, what is he saying? 'On me, this matter.'

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, כִּי קָאָמַר ״עָלַי״ — בְּהָא מִילְּתָא.
phrases.english: Here too, when he says 'on me,' he means this matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's reading from step 16
steps.raayaObject: 'עָלַי' can be explaining wording and not a new commitment
steps.raayaSupportSource: The half-נזיר case in the next משנה, where there is only one thing to accept

steps.title: רבא: a משנה would not add extra words in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the two cases are not the same. Extra words in the half-נזיר case make sense only to match the first case, where they are needed. If they were not needed in either case, the משנה would not include them in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: How can you compare them?! If the words are needed in the first case and not needed in the later case, fine: the later case was taught with extra words to match the first case, which needs them. But if you say they are not needed in either case, would the משנה teach both cases with words that are not needed?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב הונא's proof and keeps his own reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה sometimes copies wording into a later case just to match an earlier case. That explains the extra 'עָלַי' in the half-נזיר case. But it only works if the words were really needed in the first case, which proves that 'וַאֲנִי' there covered only the first half.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רֵישָׁא' means our case (the full נזיר) and 'סֵיפָא' means the half-נזיר case, not the two halves of the man's statement as in step 14.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's reading stands: 'וַאֲנִי' covers only the first part, becoming a נזיר. Taking on the payment needs the friend's own 'עָלַי'.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: How can you compare them?!
It makes sense if you say
that the first case needs it and the later case does not —
he taught the later case that does not need it
because of the first case that does need it.
But if you say

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא לָא צְרִיכָא סֵיפָא לָא צְרִיכָא,
phrases.english: that the first case does not need it and the later case does not need it,

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רֵישָׁא דְּלָא צְרִיכָא וְתָנֵי סֵיפָא דְּלָא צְרִיכָא?!
phrases.english: would he teach a first case that does not need it and a later case that does not need it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's proof from step 17 and restores רבא's reading
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב הונא's proof from the half-נזיר case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Extra words in a later case can be explained by matching the earlier case, but extra words in both cases cannot be explained

steps.title: A new teaching begins: a man speaking to his messenger
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר יוסף quotes רבי יוחנן about someone who tells his messenger something. The rest of the teaching comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: One who says to his messenger...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and starts a teaching of רבי יוחנן. This line only sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words are here: a case where a man gives instructions to his messenger. The actual case and ruling follow in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: His messenger, someone sent to act for him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who says to his messenger

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of 'וַאֲנִי' ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated; the case of a man and his messenger is only being introduced
